kill_fact: No single fact fully breaks the bear thesis, so not REFUTED; the bear's STRUCTURAL claims are confirmed by primary sources and are getting WORSE, not better. The autonomous-mobility disintermediation the bear warns about is no longer hypothetical: YipitData shows Waymo has already SURPASSED Lyft to become San Francisco's #2 ride-hail service (Waymo >25% share, Lyft down toward ~22-30%), the exact lead-market template the secular playbook says to watch. The Nashville launch (Apr 2026) dispatches Waymo-app-FIRST with Lyft second, confirming Lyft does NOT own the demand relationship in the AV future. Wedbush downgraded LYFT explicitly on robotaxi disruption risk and the stock is -26% YTD 2026 - the 'fear-print' multiple is the market pricing a melting #2, not a mispricing. The GAAP 'mirage' is confirmed: FY2025 net income's $2.84B is driven by a one-time $2.9B deferred-tax valuation-allowance release (10-K), and real profitability is a thin 2.7% adjusted-EBITDA margin on gross bookings (Q1'26). A low multiple on an eroding, no-pricing-power #2 whose terminal value is now visibly contracting in the AV lead market is a value trap, as the bear argues.
corrections: Two load-bearing balance-sheet numbers in the thesis were wrong - and both cut FOR the company, strengthening only the downside floor, not the terminal case. (1) Net cash is ~$734M, NOT $465M: per the Q1'26 release, cash+ST-investments $1,720.9M less long-term debt $986.6M = $734.3M. (2) Debt is ~$987M, NOT $1.26B. (3) TTM FCF is $1,122.1M, NOT $1.16B (overstated ~3%). (4) Diluted share count is 402.5M, NOT ~430M. Note a real, un-flagged item: a $450M convertible senior note due 2030 (priced Sep 2025, capped-call-mitigated) sits inside that debt - a latent dilution layer the bull SoP ignored. Net effect: the FCF + net-cash DOWNSIDE FLOOR is genuine and even firmer than stated, so the bear's 'downside is small / largely in the stock' sub-claim holds; but none of this rehabilitates the eroding-moat terminal case.
evidence: Lyft Q1 2026 press release (investor.lyft.com, 2026-05-07): TTM FCF $1,122.1M; cash+ST-inv $1,720.9M; long-term debt $986.6M (net cash $734.3M); adjusted EBITDA $132.8M at only 2.7% of gross bookings; 402.5M diluted shares; $300M Q1'26 buyback.

Lyft FY2025 10-K / Annual Report (SEC EDGAR, CIK 0001759509): FY2025 GAAP net income includes a one-time $2.9B benefit from releasing the U.S. federal/state deferred-tax valuation allowance in Q4'25 - confirming the 45% net margin / $6.81 EPS headline is a non-operating accounting artifact.
